title: Wolf and Crown Again
premise: Paloma Blackwood, last apprentice of the smugglers' guild that once ruled the Thornfell passes, takes in a mute child who speaks a language older than any kingdom—and discovers the boy is a vessel for the sealed memory of the Wolf-Kings, whose war with the Crown shattered the mountains a thousand years ago. As royal hunters close in and Paloma's own guild-brothers betray him for a pardon, he must choose between handing over the child to save his found family or revealing the truth: that the Crown's founding legitimacy rests on a stolen crown and a genocide buried beneath Thornfell. In the end, Paloma leads the child to the deep vault where the old kings sleep, wakes them not as conquerors but as witnesses, and forces the young queen to kneel before history itself—dissolving her absolute power into a shared covenant, while Paloma's ragtag found family becomes the first free company of the new mountain compact.
about_author: Lior Quintana is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping remote mountain communities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about borders—geographic, linguistic, and moral—from a small house at the edge of a range much like Thornfell.

chapters.title: The Last Tollhouse
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He runs the final smuggling route of a dying guild, paying off debts and dodging the queen's new road wardens. Emotional beat: weary pride in a craft everyone says is finished.

chapters.title: A Knock in Dead Winter
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A half-frozen child appears at the tollhouse door during a blizzard, speaking no known tongue yet drawing maps of roads Paloma alone knows. Beat: reluctant wonder cracking his isolation.

chapters.title: Words Older than Stone
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The guild's blind archivist, Maren, recognizes fragments of the boy's speech as pre-kingdom Thornic. Beat: dread—the language was erased on purpose.

chapters.title: The Guild Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She shows Paloma the guild's true founding charter: they were once the Wolf-Kings' road-wardens, sworn to guard something beneath the peaks. Beat: inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Riders in Grey
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Crown inquisitors arrive searching for 'a stolen vessel,' offering gold for informants. Beat: fear sharpening into defiance.

chapters.title: What the Boy Dreams
chapters.summary: Child's POV (rendered through Paloma's observation). The boy sleepwalks, singing songs that make the hearth-flames bow. Beat: tenderness mixed with terror.

chapters.title: Brothers at the Table
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He gathers the three remaining guild members—gruff Ferro, sharp-tongued Isolde, and drunk old Tam—to vote on hiding the child. Beat: fragile solidarity.

chapters.title: The Queen's Warrant
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vael's POV. We see the hunt from the other side: Vael genuinely believes the child is a weapon of the old blood. Beat: chilling conviction.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Roads
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The company flees through hidden passes only Paloma can navigate, pursued by warden patrols. Beat: exhilaration of mastery under pressure.

chapters.title: Isolde's Price
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She secretly sends word to a royal contact, weighing her sister's imprisonment against the guild's oath. Beat: corrosive divided loyalty.

chapters.title: The Hollow Chapel
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Sheltering in an abandoned shrine, they find murals of crowned wolves slaughtered by men holding a broken crown. Beat: history rewriting itself before their eyes.

chapters.title: Tam Talks Too Much
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Drunk in a border town, he brags about 'a treasure under Thornfell'; a listener pays him in silver. Beat: guilt and foreshadowing.

chapters.title: Vael Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. Using Tam's slip and Isolde's letter, Vael triangulates their route. Beat: the hunter becoming sympathetic even as he closes in.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Wardens ambush them; Tam dies buying time, and Paloma realizes someone inside sold them out. Beat: grief fused with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Child Speaks
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cornered, the boy speaks his first common words: 'They are waking.' His eyes flash amber. Beat: awe tipping into fear of the child himself.

chapters.title: Ferro's Doubt
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. He argues for giving up the boy before they all die for a stranger. Beat: loyalty strained to its breaking point.

chapters.title: The Deep Road
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They descend into the smugglers' oldest tunnel, which Maren's charts say predates the guild itself. Beat: claustrophobic descent into the past.

chapters.title: Bones of the Wardens
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They find the original guild dead in formation, guarding a sealed door, still holding their pikes after a thousand years. Beat: solemn inheritance of duty.

chapters.title: Isolde Confesses
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. She admits her betrayal—not for gold, but because Vael holds her sister. Beat: forgiveness offered but not yet earned.

chapters.title: The Vault Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The door answers the boy's song, grinding open onto darkness and cold air that smells of snow and iron. Beat: threshold terror.

chapters.title: What Sleeps Below
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Inside: not monsters, but sleeping Wolf-Kings preserved in ice-glass, and the true crown of Thornfell on a stone table. Beat: revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: Vael's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. He corners them at the vault mouth, offering amnesty for all if the child is surrendered. Beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Ferro steps aside; Isolde stands with Paloma; Paloma refuses, and Vael orders the vault stormed. Beat: commitment despite cost.

chapters.title: Battle in the Dark
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Fighting by torchlight among the tombs; Maren is gravely wounded shielding the boy. Beat: sacrifice and chaos.

chapters.title: The Waking
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The boy completes his purpose—he is the memory-vessel—and the first Wolf-King opens her eyes. Beat: sublime, terrifying wonder.

chapters.title: Audience with Ash
chapters.summary: Wolf-King Sera's POV. Ancient, lucid, furious, she reads the room: these small mortals did not come to worship or to steal. Beat: judgment suspended.

chapters.title: The Stolen Crown
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. She reveals the truth: the royal line's crown was forged from hers, its authority built on the massacre the guild was founded to hide. Beat: the ground of the world shifting.

chapters.title: Retreat Above Ground
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They escape the collapsing vault with Sera and the boy, leaving Vael buried-but-alive below. Beat: battered survival, uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: Sera Among Mortals
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. The ancient king experiences hunger, cold, and Ferro's grudging kindness. Beat: humanity seen through immortal eyes.

chapters.title: March on Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They travel to the provincial capital, gathering smugglers, miners, and deserters who have grievances against the Crown. Beat: hope assembling into a movement.

chapters.title: Vael Unburied
chapters.summary: Vael's POV. Dug out by his own wardens, half-mad, he reports to the young Queen Aurelian that the Wolf-Kings live. Beat: panic at the heart of power.

chapters.title: The Queen's Fear
chapters.summary: Queen Aurelian's POV. Told the truth of her crown's origin, she must choose between destroying the evidence and facing it. Beat: corruption tempting a decent ruler.

chapters.title: Parley at the Pass
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Aurelian offers Paloma everything—pardon, guild restored, wealth—for Sera's head. Beat: the same choice again, now with a crown's price tag.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He refuses publicly before both armies, telling the assembled soldiers what the murals and the vault showed. Beat: truth as a weapon sharper than steel.

chapters.title: Battle of Thornfell Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Aurelian, cornered by her council, attacks; the battle teeters until Sera refuses to fight, standing unarmed between the lines. Beat: climax of moral force over force.

chapters.title: The Kneeling
chapters.summary: Aurelian's POV. Broken by the revealed truth and her soldiers' wavering, she kneels to Sera—not in conquest, but in acknowledgment. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: The Mountain Compact
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera declines a throne; instead she dictates a covenant splitting power among crown, guilds, and mountain clans, then chooses to return to sleep, leaving the boy as living witness. Beat: wisdom renouncing power.

chapters.title: What the Guild Becomes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The smugglers' guild is reborn as the wardens of the compact, roads opened lawful for the first time in centuries. Beat: quiet pride, identity transformed.

chapters.title: Isolde's Sister
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Her sister is freed; Isolde asks Paloma for a place in the new guild and receives it without conditions. Beat: forgiveness completed.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Epilogue: the boy, learning common speech, chooses to stay with Paloma rather than serve as a relic; together they watch the first free caravans cross Thornfell. Beat: found family sealed, dawn after the long winter.
